A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DBP robustness study and ADDT method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including content relocated between appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original robustness experiments, ADDT evaluations, ablations, and attack-trajectory analyses in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds perturbation analyses, training controls, and further deterministic white-box evaluations in Appendices K and M.

M1.justification: ADDT retains the same alternating CGPO and diffusion-training procedure, RBGM mapping, noise mixture, and objectives. Section 5.1 now identifies the gradient bypass as BPDA and clarifies its training-only use; v2 already describes the corresponding gradient transfer, and Algorithm 1 remains procedurally equivalent.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1k coverage is retained. Appendix K.2 adds a focused input-corruption scenario: directly testing a clean WRN-28-10 classifier with Gaussian versus RBGM-mapped perturbations. The other additions primarily concern controls and model configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The existing DBP comparator set is unchanged. Appendix K.4 introduces an L2-normalized perturbation training comparator against ADDT in Tables 19–20, plus a Gaussian-reordered perturbation training control against vanilla training in Table 18.

E3.justification: The retained benchmark attack budgets, perturbation bounds, sample counts, and training settings remain unchanged. New Appendix K experiments specify direct perturbation scaling of 0.03, zero-mean/unit-variance normalization for the reordered control, and matching perturbation L2 norms. These are protocols for added analyses, rather than revisions to the existing evaluations.

E4.justification: New Appendix K substantially expands validation of RBGM through distribution comparisons across images, timesteps, and mixtures; a test of retained adversarial potency; and reordered-value and L2-normalized training controls. Appendix M additionally tests deterministic white-box robustness of DiffPure and EDM. The earlier L-infinity perturbation ablation and AutoAttack analyses are retained elsewhere.

E5.justification: Neither version provides quantitative repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and no new seed or run-count reporting is introduced. Appendix P retains the independent implementation and verification statement. The new perturbation-distribution plots examine noise characteristics rather than uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, but v3 adds substantial results about perturbation design and deterministic robustness. Table 17 reports 81.54% classifier accuracy with Gaussian noise versus 4.47% with RBGM perturbations; Table 20 adds an L2-normalized control FID of 5.678 versus ADDT's retained 5.190. Table 22 newly reports vanilla/ADDT DW-box accuracies of 22.76%/51.63% for DiffPure and 13.33%/32.94% for EDM. These are added comparisons, not improvements over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix K.3 adds a short derivation connecting image-space adversarial perturbations to diffusion-noise perturbations and deriving the existing time-dependent scaling factor gamma_t (Equations 21–24). The core objectives and diffusion equations remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: stochasticity primarily explains DBP robustness, DW-box evaluation exposes limited purification capability, and ADDT with RBGM improves purification-based robustness. Rewriting and additional supporting evidence do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix K clarifies that RBGM matches distributions of perturbation values without guaranteeing a joint multivariate Gaussian, and proposes statistical consistency and reduced image dependence as benefits. It also interprets the new normalization controls. Appendix O newly interprets existing accelerated results as potential inference savings; the main stochasticity interpretation and stated limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix P changes a promised ADDT code release into a statement that a public repository is available. The AutoAttack disclosure changes from an anonymous location to a named repository. Section 5.1 more explicitly documents PGD/BPDA handling and its training-only role. These improve documented access and implementation clarity without establishing changes to the underlying procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds Athalye et al.'s Synthesizing Robust Adversarial Examples for EoT and Huang et al.'s Revisiting Residual Networks for Adversarial Robustness for the scaling discussion. References to Song and Ermon (2019) and Krizhevsky et al. (2009) disappear. The broader positioning relative to adversarial training and purification remains stable; publication-metadata updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main text and appendices undergo extensive sentence and paragraph rewriting. AutoAttack discussion moves from Appendix L to E.1, the earlier RBGM evaluation moves from K to L, and a structured RBGM discussion occupies K. Author information, publication headers, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds distribution Figures 9–10 and new experimental tables, redraws the ADDT overview in Figure 4, and consolidates the earlier two-panel NFE robustness plot into Figure 11. It also transposes the sensitivity table and rearranges several main-text and appendix tables. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the rationale for RBGM with useful normalization controls, perturbation analyses, and clearer qualification of its Gaussian properties, while extending DW-box evidence and reporting ADDT code access. These improve support and reproducibility of the existing contribution. The gain is a focused strengthening rather than a fundamental correction: the core method, claims, and benchmark results remain intact, and the added comparisons provide no uncertainty estimates.
